_doc: The IMR instance's fish layer (tools/instance.json layer.fish; design note docs/reviews/2026-11-14-sheet-overlay-design.md v2, step 5): what IMR decides about its fish content, laid on tools/fish_source.json (the sources' part) by tools/build_fish.py through tools/instance.py fish_source. Edit this file, then re-run the build: python3 tools/build_fish.py --regroup (offline) is enough for cues, look, phase, start and the look groups; a circle needs the full build. The content editor's edits are not here: curation.json content, laid over at load (rule A1). Layout: tools/instance.py layer_dumps (one node per line).

start: the starter core, the circle-1 entries a new player meets first, before any other opens (model.js openPick, a record's first). Pierre's fish-ID design (2026-11-04): four easy, readable families first, Butterflyfishes, Angelfishes, Damselfishes & Anemonefishes, Surgeonfishes & Tangs.

look: look-alike groups of the book's families declared beyond the IMR course, each {src, key (the key whose family labels the ids name: applied only while it is in force), groups [[family ids]], note {"a|b": words}}: every pair of a group is a look-alike both ways, its source in the families' lsrc (tools/build_fish.py add_families). Pierre, 2026-11-06, from experience; they seed the traps and the confusion groups until pooled fish answers exist.
nodes: {teaching node or sub-entry id (tools/fish_source.json teach, sub): its fields}. A node or sub-entry the source does not hold stops the build.
circle (teaching nodes only; a species takes its node's circle, Q214): 1 IMR core, 2 seen sometimes on SVS video, 3 opt-in beyond IMR; absent: 1.
cues, look ([teach id, how to tell it apart]), phase: short English from the IMR fish presentation (its slides: the source's sl).
